items.title: Kildunne returns to haunt Harlequins as Bristol get PWR season off to a flyer
items.desc:
• Harlequins 21-48 Bristol

  • Full-back marks debut with two tries against former club

As women’s rugby grows, more scrutiny will follow and Ellie Kildunne has felt that over the past few months. Her performances have been put under a microscope after being dropped to the bench in England’s final two WXV matches in October, but she silenced her critics with a stellar and trademark performance in her club debut for Bristol. The full-back did it under significant pressure, too, as she returned to the Stoop five months after her shock exit from Harlequins and helped Bristol beat her former side in their Premiership Women’s Rugby opener.

The Bristol head coach, Scott Lawson, had thrown his full backing behind Kildunne in the buildup, saying that being at the West Country club would “bring the best” out of the 27-year-old and if her debut is anything to go by he will be proved right. The World Cup winner not only scored two tries but was also a linchpin in Bristol’s attack. Her attacking prowess and gamechanging reputation was felt among her former teammates as she drew multiple players to her whenever she had the ball, meaning the wings on her outside had a lot more joy. The back three looked formidable with both wings, Reneeqa Bonner and Millie David, also scoring two tries apiece.

items.title: Steve Borthwick hits rewind button to inspire England’s flying starts
items.desc:
The head coach said he has watched videos from Eddie Jones’ time in charge to help England start matches strongly

Ellis Genge was so fired up by England’s powerful response to the haka on Saturday he stripped off his anthem jacket in the aftermath, completely forgetting he was not starting. Ollie Chessum told Lewis Moody, who had been invited to stand at the point of England’s V formation, “we are going long left, stay on the field and chase the kick-off”. And according to Ben Earl, who would still be out on the Twickenham turf carrying through traffic if he could, some players were so inspired by Moody’s speech the night before they could not sleep.

Against that emotional backdrop, it is small wonder England flew out of the blocks against the All Blacks. Steve Borthwick has spoken a lot about “bringing the fire” recently and on Saturday they torched the place, riding the emotional wave that Moody’s presence inspired from Henry Slade’s fourth-minute try, through to a record victory against New Zealand.
